keyVerseText: And Moses said, Thus saith the LORD, About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt:
rootMeaning: The root of חָצוֹת (châtsôwth) comes from חָצָה (châtsâh), which means to divide or cut in two. This etymology highlights the concept of a division or midpoint, emphasizing a literal splitting or halving. Thus, beyond the common English gloss of 'midnight,' the root sense conveys the idea of a precise division in time, the exact middle point of the night, rather than just a vague late hour.
usageInScripture: This word appears three times in the Hebrew Bible and is consistently translated as 'midnight' or 'at midnight,' indicating a very specific time frame: the middle of the night. The uniformity in translation underscores its clear meaning as a temporal marker rather than a metaphorical or symbolic term. Its use in phrases like חֲצֹת הַלַּיְלָה (midnight) shows it functions primarily as an adverbial phrase indicating the exact middle of the night.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding חָצוֹת as the exact midpoint of night enriches our grasp of biblical events that occur at this hour, often moments of divine intervention or judgment. It highlights God's sovereign control over time and history, pinpointing the moment when His purposes unfold decisively. For the Christian faith, this reminds believers that God’s timing is perfect and precise, working even in the darkest hours to accomplish His will. The concept of division or midpoint can also spiritually symbolize the breaking point between darkness and the coming of light, a theme fulfilled ultimately in Christ, the light of the world.
keyVerseReflection: In Exodus 11:4, Moses declares that the LORD will go out 'about midnight' into Egypt, signaling a pivotal moment of divine judgment. The use of חָצוֹת here emphasizes the exactness and inevitability of God's action at the very center of the night, a time when all is quiet and vulnerable. This word underscores the seriousness and precision of God's timing in delivering His people and executing His justice, reminding us that God's plans unfold according to His perfect schedule.
